sources.excerpt: The Wampler Pantheon Deluxe is a versatile dual overdrive pedal, offering a wide range of tones from creamy gain to heavy distortion. It features two independent channels, one emulating a classic Blues Breaker circuit and the other a modern boutique sound. With dual inputs/outputs, and MIDI channel switching, the Pantheon Deluxe provides extensive tone-shaping options, making it a must-have for guitarists seeking a comprehensive overdrive solution. What Wampler Pedals say about the Pantheon Deluxe The now legendary Wampler Pantheon provided a unique interpretation of the classic “Blues Breaker” style stomp box, by capturing all the tonal nuance of the original, but with added flexibility and style. In doing so, it found its way onto thousands of pedalboards across the world. Enter the new Pantheon Deluxe – a dual overdrive pedal that takes this evolution several steps further by offering a flexible design with two completely independent Pantheon circuits, one voiced as a classic blues breaker and one with a more modern boutique sound. This palace of tone delivers a staggering 200 combinations of gain settings, featuring dual Inputs and Outputs, and for the first time ever, Wampler have added MIDI channel switching to one of their gain pedals. The Pantheon Deluxe lets you dial in two channels of organic creamy gain, gritty overdrive, or heavy distortion while retaining Wampler’s famous ease of use and flexibility. Channel 1 delivers a classic Blues Breaker tone, Channel 2 is a recreation of the original Pantheon, a similar circuit to the Blues Breaker but with a modern boutique feel. Independent side mounted Voicing and Gain Level switches allow you to further shape your tone to perfection. www.wamplerpedals.com What guitarists say... Guitarists found the Wampler Pantheon Deluxe to be incredibly versatile, capable of producing a wide array of tones from low-gain smoothness to high-gain distortion. Users praised its tweakability, MIDI integration, and ability to work well with different amplifiers and other pedals. While some noted a slight noise increase at high gain settings, the overall consensus was overwhelmingly positive, with many considering it a pedal they would keep on their board for years.
